previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with critical aortic stenosis, severe diastolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted after two falls and found to be hypotensive with severe anemia (hemoglobin 4.4 g/dL) due to a gastrointestinal bleed. He was transfused three units of packed red blood cells and stabilized. Evaluation revealed a positive H. pylori infection, and he was treated with quadruple therapy. An endoscopy showed gastritis and erosions but no active bleeding source. Due to high bleeding risk, warfarin was discontinued and replaced with aspirin. He developed transient acute kidney injury and mild pulmonary edema, both of which resolved with careful diuresis management. A left olecranon fracture was managed nonoperatively. He improved steadily, was weaned off oxygen, and transitioned to extended care with stable vital signs and hemoglobin of 9.1 g/dL at discharge.
problems: Closed fracture of olecranon process of ulna
Severe chronic diastolic congestive heart failure

Brief Hospital Course:
BRIEF SUMMARY STATEMENT:  Mr. ___ is a ___ y/o M PMH 
significant for afib (no longer on coumadin after recent GIB), 
diastolic CHF, critical AS, and recent admission for hemorrhagic 
shock secondary to GIB (EGD done showing gastritis) who presents 
with 1 episode of BRBPR.  Pt. had flex sigmoidoscopy done by GI 
which revealed grade 3 internal hemorrhoids with stigmata of 
recent bleeding.  Pt. remained stable throughout 
hospitalization.  He required no pRBC transfusions.  He was 
discharged back to rehab with close outpatient follow-up.  

ACTIVE ISSUES
=============

# BRBPR:  Pt with 1 episode of BRBPR at rehab.  Given hx. of 
recent GIB leading to hemorrhagic shock, pt. presented to the 
___ ED immediately from rehab.  Pt. remained hemodynamically 
stable throughout admission and was noted to be near his 
baseline hematocrit.  He required no pRBC transfusions during 
admission.  GI evaluated the pt. and after discussion with pt's 
son (the HCP), it was decided for pt. to undergo flex 
sigmoidoscopy.  Flex sig revealed grade 3 internal hemorrhoids 
with stigmata of recent bleeding.  This was thought to be the 
culprit lesion.  Post-procedure,  pt. remained stable and was 
discharged back to rehab.  He was instructed to continue with 
daily anusol suppositories and ___ baths. 

# ___:  Thought to be ___ pre-renal etiology in the setting of 
GI bleed and ongoing baseline diuresis.  Temporarily held pt's 
diuretics and encouraged PO.  Pt's creatinine returned to 
baseline (baseline creatinine 0.9-1.2).  

# Anemia:  Pt with chronic anemia with baseline hemoglobin 7.5 
to 9.5.  On admission, Hgb noted at 7.9.  He remained near this 
RBC level throughout admission.  

# L elbow nondisplaced olecranon fracture:  Pt. with recent 
nondisplaced left olecranon fracture that continues to slowly 
heal.  Pt. recently saw orthopedic surgery on ___.  
Management of his olecranon fracture was continued based on that 
visit's recommendations including non-weight bearing in left UE, 
continue wearing Orthoplast splint on left elbow at all times 
other than with ___, limit ROM of left elbow to 90 degrees, 
and ongoing work with ___ consult.  Pt. refused to wear brace 
intermittently during visit.  He reported no significant pain 
with the elbow over the course of his hospitalization.

CHRONIC ISSUES
==============

# Gastritis:  Stable.  Continued on BID omeprazole.

# Afib:  Pt. with CHADS2 of 5.  Given recent significant GIB, it 
was decided that pt. should be discontinued off of coumadin.  He 
was continued on rate/rhythm control with amio and digoxin.  

# Diastolic CHF:  Pt. with chronic severe diastolic CHF.  He was 
recently taken off metoprolol.  His diuretic regimen was resumed 
at discharge.  

# Severe Aortic Stenosis:  Stable.  Diuretic regimen resumed at 
discharge.

# CAD:  Stable.  Continue on ASA and crestor.

# Constipation:  Stable.  Continued on aggressive bowel regemin.

# Chronic Pain:  Stable.  Continue on standing tylenol, 
tramadol, PRN lidocaine, and QHS gabapentin.

# BPH:  Stable.  Continue tamuslosin.

# HLD:  Stable.  Continue on crestor.

# COPD:  Stable.  Continued on home regimen including 
fluticasone-Salmeterol, tiotropium, and duonebs PRN.

# Vitamin D Deficiency:  Stable.  Continued on vitamin D 
supplementation.

====================

repeat episode, would consider colorectal surgery visit to

suppository and ___ baths.
